summary: Multi-phase bitmap pixel decompression. The info struct (a1) carries a phase byte (this+0x8), a sub-state byte (this+0x9, bit depth or chroma-key index width), an output bytes-per-pixel byte (this+0xA), an output stride byte (this+0xB), a pixel count (this+0x0), and a byte-count/pointer field (this+0x4). Phase 0 unpacks 1/2/4-bit packed pixels into full bytes (scaling the optional key color a3[4] by 255/85/17) and then applies a chroma-key alpha pass (8-bit or 16-bit key width), writing 2 or 4 bytes per pixel and finalizing phase to 4. Phase 2 applies direct chroma-key conversion for 8-bit or 16-bit index formats, writing 4 or 8 bytes per pixel and finalizing phase to 6. Other phase values are a no-op. Returns the pixel count.

operations.description: Guard on phase byte (this+0x8): zero selects the bit-unpacking phase, value 2 selects the direct-color chroma-key phase, and any other value falls through as a no-op returning the pixel count.
Guard: phase == 2 and a chroma-key word table a3 non-null enters direct-color conversion; the key width is read from sub-state byte this+0x9.
Guard: sub-state == 8 selects the 8-bit-index chroma-key path, comparing three consecutive source bytes against the key words a3[1], a3[2], a3[3].

8-bit path: for each of count pixels (this+0x0), scan backward from a2 + 4*count - 1 and emit 4 output bytes: an alpha byte (0x00 when the three source bytes match the key words, else 0xFF) followed by the three copied color bytes.
Guard: sub-state == 16 selects the 16-bit-index chroma-key path, assembling three words from six source bytes and comparing them against a3[1], a3[2], a3[3].

16-bit path: for each of count pixels (this+0x0), scan backward from a2 + 8*count - 1 and emit 8 output bytes: two alpha bytes (0x00 when the three source words match the key words, else 0xFF) followed by the six copied color bytes.
Phase-2 tail: mark completion by setting this+0x8 = 6, this+0xA = 4 (bytes per pixel), this+0xB = 4 * sub-state, and this+0x4 = (count * this+0xB) >> 3.
Guard: phase 0 and sub-state this+0x9 < 8 enters the bit-unpacking phase; when a3 is non-null the key color word is loaded from a3[4].
Guard: sub-state == 1 selects the 1-bit unpack path, in which the key color is scaled by 255 and each packed bit expands to a 0x00 or 0xFF byte.
1-bit path: iterate count pixels (this+0x0), reading each bit from the packed source at a running bit index and writing the expanded byte, walking pointers backward from a2 + count - 1.
Guard: sub-state == 2 selects the 2-bit unpack path, in which the key color is scaled by 85 and each 2-bit value is replicated four times to fill a byte.
2-bit path: iterate count pixels (this+0x0), reading each 2-bit value from the packed source and writing the replicated byte, walking pointers backward from a2 + count - 1.
Guard: sub-state == 4 selects the 4-bit unpack path, in which the key color is scaled by 17 and each nibble is duplicated to fill a byte.
4-bit path: iterate count pixels (this+0x0), reading each nibble from the packed source and writing the duplicated byte, walking pointers backward from a2 + count - 1.
After unpacking: set sub-state this+0x9 = 8, stride this+0xB = 8, and row byte count this+0x4 = count.
Guard: second chroma-key pass on the unpacked row when a3 is non-null; sub-state == 8 selects a single-byte key compare and == 16 selects a two-byte word compare.
8-bit chroma pass: compare each unpacked byte against the key color, writing an alpha byte (0x00 on match else 0xFF) plus the color byte, emitting 2 output bytes per pixel.
16-bit chroma pass: compare each two-byte word against the key color, writing two alpha bytes (0x00 on match else 0xFF) plus the two color bytes, emitting 4 output bytes per word.
Chroma-key tail: mark completion by setting this+0x8 = 4, this+0xA = 2 (bytes per pixel), this+0xB = 2 * sub-state, and this+0x4 = (count * this+0xB) >> 3.
Return the pixel count read from this+0x0 at entry.
